I recently had Al Tazaj in Makkah, and I must say it was delicious. I ordered the Forge dish, and it was absolutely tasty—perfectly juicy with a delightful hint of lemon that added a refreshing twist to every bite. The flavors were well-balanced, and the quality of the food really stood out.

Although it’s primarily a take-out spot, there are plenty of tables and chairs nearby, making it convenient to sit down and enjoy the meal right away. Whether you’re looking for a quick bite or a satisfying meal, Al Tazaj is definitely a place worth visiting in Makkah. I’ll be coming back for more of that incredible taste!

Al Tazaj is a restaurant known for its broast and sandwiches, offering a solid dining experience for those who enjoy these dishes. I tried their broast, and it was good—crispy, flavorful, and well-cooked. However, when compared to the renowned Al Baik, I wouldn’t say it surpasses it. While some people argue that Al Tazaj is better, I personally find Al Baik’s taste more appealing, especially considering the price difference.

One standout aspect of Al Tazaj is its excellent staff. The team is extremely cooperative and manages a massive crowd efficiently, which is no small feat. Their ability to maintain quality service despite the rush is commendable and adds to the overall dining experience.

However, the pricing is on the higher side compared to Al Baik, making it less economical. For me, the combination of affordability and taste at Al Baik gives it an edge.

Overall, Al Tazaj offers good food, excellent service, and a pleasant atmosphere, but it may not be the first choice for those looking for value-for-money options. It’s a nice spot to visit if you’re in the mood for quality broast and don’t mind the slightly higher price tag.

Starting with the burger itself, the presentation was decent. It came nicely assembled, and the portion size was quite satisfying. The bun was soft and fresh, holding everything together well. However, the patty was a bit oilier than I expected. While a juicy burger is always welcome, this one leaned a little too much towards being greasy rather than just moist.

The flavor was not bad at all. The burger had a noticeable grilled taste, which added a nice smoky touch. It wasn’t the most unique or mind-blowing flavor I’ve had in a burger, but it was enjoyable. The seasoning was balanced, though I feel it could have used a little extra seasoning or sauce to elevate it further. If you enjoy a classic grilled burger, you’ll probably like this one.

The ingredients were fresh. The lettuce was crisp, the tomatoes were ripe, and the cheese was nicely melted over the patty. I appreciated that the toppings weren’t overwhelming or messy, which made it easier to eat without everything falling apart. However, the oiliness of the patty did make it a little heavy.

As for the service, the staff was friendly and efficient. My order didn’t take too long, and the place had a casual, comfortable vibe. It’s a good spot if you’re looking for a quick, simple burger without too much fuss.

Would I recommend Peak Burger? Yes, but with some expectations in mind. If you’re looking for a fancy gourmet burger, this might not be the place for you. But if you just want a solid, grilled burger with decent flavor, it’s a good option. I’d rate it 4 stars because while it was enjoyable, the oiliness could be improved, and the flavor, while good, wasn’t particularly special.

Would I return? Probably, but I might try a different burger next time to see if there’s one that stands out more.

I had a great time eating the delicious Peak burger. The burger had a nice smoky flavor, and the sauce was just right—not too much, so you could really taste the burger itself. Although the market changes and prices go up, I like that they have maintained the same quality of the burger.

I have been to the peak multiple times so here’s my review:

Atmosphere: 4.5/5
The rooftop setting offers breathtaking views of the city, especially at sunset. The ambiance is upscale yet relaxed, making it an ideal spot for both casual outings and special occasions. The modern décor and comfortable seating enhance the overall experience.

Food: 4/5
The Peak offers a diverse menu with a mix of international dishes, including steak, seafood, and pasta. While the food is generally well-received, some diners feel that the pricing could be a bit high for the portion sizes. However, the quality of ingredients is commendable.

Service: 4/5
The staff are usually attentive and friendly. Guests appreciate the professionalism of the service team, though during busy times, there can be slight delays in getting orders to the table.

Value for Money: 3.5/5
Given the premium location and ambiance, prices are on the higher side. While the experience is worth it for the views and atmosphere, some might find it slightly overpriced compared to other dining options in Al Khobar.

Overall: 4/5
The peak is an excellent choice for those looking to enjoy a luxurious rooftop dining experience with beautiful views. It's perfect for a special night out, though it might not be the most budget-friendly option in town.

I recently visited Peak Burger and decided to try their special Peak Burger, which seems to be their signature item. Overall, the experience was good, but there were a few things that could have been better.

Starting with the burger itself, the presentation was decent. It came nicely assembled, and the portion size was quite satisfying. The bun was soft and fresh, holding everything together well. However, the patty was a bit oilier than I expected. While a juicy burger is always welcome, this one leaned a little too much towards being greasy rather than just moist.

The flavor was not bad at all. The burger had a noticeable grilled taste, which added a nice smoky touch. It wasn’t the most unique or mind-blowing flavor I’ve had in a burger, but it was enjoyable. The seasoning was balanced, though I feel it could have used a little extra seasoning or sauce to elevate it further. If you enjoy a classic grilled burger, you’ll probably like this one.

The ingredients were fresh. The lettuce was crisp, the tomatoes were ripe, and the cheese was nicely melted over the patty. I appreciated that the toppings weren’t overwhelming or messy, which made it easier to eat without everything falling apart. However, the oiliness of the patty did make it a little heavy.

As for the service, the staff was friendly and efficient. My order didn’t take too long, and the place had a casual, comfortable vibe. It’s a good spot if you’re looking for a quick, simple burger without too much fuss.

Would I recommend Peak Burger? Yes, but with some expectations in mind. If you’re looking for a fancy gourmet burger, this might not be the place for you. But if you just want a solid, grilled burger with decent flavor, it’s a good option. I’d rate it 4 stars because while it was enjoyable, the oiliness could be improved, and the flavor, while good, wasn’t particularly special.

Would I return? Probably, but I might try a different burger next time to see if there’s one that stands out more.
